question: GQ-006
action: open every remaining unbacked database instead of ranking them by guesswork
motivation: Last loop I called books.sqlite low-value because no claim cited it, then found it was the bibliographic catalogue. The ranking was backwards: nothing cited it because I had not looked inside. So I looked inside all twelve.

error_14_group.diagnosis: All healthy. write_version 2 (WAL); they open fine with immutable=1 and hold 12, 12, 2 and 8 tables.
error_14_group.note: Same failure mode as the vault databases. A survey without immutable=1 would have reported four healthy files as unreadable.

error_11_finding.diagnosis: GENUINELY CORRUPT. Valid SQLite header, write_version 2, but quick_check cannot run: "database disk image is malformed (11)". immutable=1 does not help — this is not the WAL case.

sibling.reading: Someone already ran a .recover on it. The recovery is only partial: every real table is EMPTY and all 7,583 salvaged rows sit in lost_and_found with anonymous c0..c57 columns across 13 root pages. quick_check ok on a database whose tables are empty is exactly the kind of green signal that means nothing.

error_11_finding.assessment: Located in usage-cache/, and its tables (logs, mcp_tool_logs, async_jobs) are Bifrost gateway staging — not Library data. No claim cites it. Recording the corruption rather than attempting a second recovery on a cache.
error_11_finding.not_done: No repair attempted. C1 forbids destructive action and a cache is not worth a risky one.
